name: Microsoft Excel
note: From the Microsoft Support article "Keyboard shortcuts in Excel", Windows and macOS tabs. The Windows "Function keys" table packs several shortcuts into one row; each is listed here as its own action using Microsoft's own description. Ribbon access keys documented as "Alt, H, A, C" are written with the leading Alt folded into the first key, which is how Excel accepts them and the only form the chord grammar allows. Where Microsoft lists two equivalent bindings the first is kept. The MacBook Fn-key alternatives Microsoft documents (Fn+Left/Right/Up/Down and Fn+Delete in place of Home/End/Page Up/Page Down/Delete-right on keyboards with no dedicated key) are now included as their own actions, since the chord grammar accepts Fn as a mac-only modifier. Omitted because the grammar cannot express them: mouse and mouse-wheel bindings (scroll horizontally with Ctrl+Shift and the wheel, move rows or cells by Shift-dragging), plain "Arrow keys" entries, numeric-keypad-only bindings, Home+Scroll Lock, and open-ended entries such as "Alt, Q, then enter the search term". Rows Microsoft writes as a family over all four directions ("Ctrl+Arrow key", "Shift+Arrow key", plain "Arrow keys") are omitted rather than expanded into four names the vendor does not use.
